problem: Prior deep-RL navigation agents (UNREAL, Mirowski et al.) learn to navigate mazes but do not read a given 2D global map, and they train and test on the same mazes. Map-based localization from first-person 3D views had not been learned end-to-end with RL and generalized to unseen, larger mazes.
motivation: Using a map to navigate unseen places is important for robotics and hard for machines. The agent does not know its position on the map, so it must localize from 3D views and an approximate compass, then plan and follow a route. The task decomposes naturally into localization, map understanding and path following, so a modular architecture with per-module losses should be trainable and debuggable.
key_idea: A modular A3C agent with a recurrent localization cell that correlates an estimated local map with the global map, a map-interpretation network with a differentiable shortest-path planner, and a reactive agent trained with intrinsic exploration and exploitation rewards.
insight: Decomposing the task into modules trained with local losses (gradients stopped at module boundaries) and using a location probability distribution to query a per-cell plan lets exploration and exploitation emerge. An uncertain location gives an uncertain short-term target direction, which drives exploration. Comparing against an agent with perfect position and optimal target direction (Fig. 7) shows the extra steps come mostly from turning to look around to localize. There is no formal module ablation.
method: Visible local map network: two CNN layers plus FC on RGB, concatenated with 3-hot discretized angle (n=30). It outputs a local map excerpt and a visible-field gate, and is trained with an L2 loss against the true visible map.

Recurrent localization cell: estimates egomotion (a 3x3 distribution), shifts and accumulates an egocentric local map, adds a trainable-weight map feedback, then convolves the local map over the rasterized global map with a softmax to get a location distribution over N cells (up to 63x63=3969).

Map interpretation network: conv layers turn the map into a 3-channel reward map (wall, free, target). A parameter-free iterative shortest-path planner (200 iterations) gives a short-term target direction (N/E/S/W) and target distance per cell. This is averaged under the location distribution.

Reactive agent: a feed-forward net on the STTD, target distance, location entropy, angle and last reward, outputting the policy and value. It gets intrinsic rewards: exploration (entropy decrease) and exploitation (egomotion aligned with STTD).

Training: A3C with 16 threads and a curriculum over maze sizes 5x5 to 13x13. Four module losses: off-policy visible-map loss, on-policy localization loss (cross-entropy, centroid distance, auxiliary local-map loss), off-policy reward-map loss, and the A3C loss. RMSprop with gradient stopping at module boundaries.

setting.backbone: Custom modular network (small CNN + FC + recurrent localization cell + MLP policy) trained with A3C from scratch
setting.training_data: 100 random DeepMind Lab mazes (20 each of 5x5 to 13x13), sampled in RL episodes, plus true discretized position and angle as supervision during training
setting.observation: first-person RGB from DeepMind Lab, approximate discretized orientation angle (compass), and a global 2D black-and-white map with a target marked
setting.action_space: low-level: move forward/backward/strafe left/right and rotate left/right, with action repeat 4
setting.privileged: Ground-truth discretized position used only as a training signal; at test time there is a given global map and an approximate compass, no position.

numbers.eval_set_note: 900 random test mazes, 100 per size 5x5 to 21x21; 4500-step limit
numbers.extra: Trained only on mazes up to 13x13; test mazes up to 21x21 are larger than any seen in training
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Percentage of targets found in the test mazes

numbers_note: Success rates come from Table 1 (percent of targets found within 4500 steps). Step counts appear only in figures (Fig. 5 and Fig. 7).
results: The agent finds 100% of targets up to 9x9 mazes and 91% in 21x21 mazes, whose navigable area is about 3x larger than any training maze. Paths are near-shortest, but many steps are spent turning to localize compared with a perfect-position agent. No external baselines are compared.
limitations: Toy grid mazes in a simulator with a compass and a clean black-and-white map; no real-robot or realistic-scene evaluation.
Training uses ground-truth position for supervision, and localization costs many extra turning steps.
There are no baseline comparisons or module ablations, and some threads overfit during training.
compares_to: Agent with perfect position and optimal short-term target direction (upper bound)
